s0101.literal: If you say the rebel villain must be destroyed before my return is heard, with high carriages one after another and flying canopies following in train—having not grasped such words, how could one jest well?
s0101.idiomatic: If you say I may return only after the rebel is destroyed, with high coaches in endless file and flying canopies in train—I do not understand such words; how could one jest at all?

s0102.literal: Fortune and adversity, order and chaos—can they be foreseen beforehand?
s0102.idiomatic: Fortune and adversity, order and chaos—who can foresee them in advance?

s0103.literal: Regular Attendant Xie is fifty-one this year; I am forty-four. Both have reached the age of knowing fate; as guests we are already at the staff-and-village years. Counting that Hou Sheng, he is only a shoulder behind.
s0103.idiomatic: Regular Attendant Xie is fifty-one this year; I am forty-four. We have both reached knowing fate; as envoys we are already at staff-and-village age. Counting that Hou fellow, he is barely a step behind us.

s0104.literal: How could the essentials of the Silver Terrace be what he has not yet learned from a master, while the recipe of the Golden Stove is what I know the secret of? I truly fear that the chrysanthemum water of Nanyang will in the end not prolong life, and the mulberry fields of the Eastern Sea will have no day to be seen again.
s0104.idiomatic: As if the Silver Terrace arts were what he had never studied, while I alone knew the Golden Stove secret! I fear Nanyang's chrysanthemum water will not prolong life after all, and the Eastern Sea's mulberry fields will never be seen again.

s0105.literal: If you take this as your argument, this is what I fail to understand—eight.
s0105.idiomatic: If that is your argument, this is what I fail to understand—the eighth point.

s0106.literal: Your pure bosom rises above common trust; your garden of books and forest of letters—from primal chaos down to You and Li, is there today anyone like me? Down to the Spring and Autumn era, it would be fitting to discuss a little.
s0106.idiomatic: Your refined mind towers above ordinary men; in books and letters—from primal chaos to the reigns of You and Li—is there anyone like me today? Even in Spring and Autumn times one might debate the point.

s0107.literal: When the Zhou royal house perished, hegemonic ways turned brutal; sometimes many factions held power, sometimes dependent ministers lacked virtue. Thus Zangsun, though possessed of rites, was turned into a prisoner and a guest of another state; the Earl of Zheng, though without fault, vainly roused the Son of Heaven's envoy to anger. The Viscount of Ji was moved to the Two Lodgings; the son of Ji was tethered for three years.
s0107.idiomatic: When the Zhou royal house fell, hegemonic power turned cruel; sometimes many hands held the government, sometimes vassal ministers lacked virtue. Zangsun had rites yet was made a prisoner and another state's guest; the Earl of Zheng was blameless yet needlessly provoked the Son of Heaven's envoy. The Viscount of Ji was lodged in the Two Pavilions; the son of Ji was bound for three years.

s0108.literal: Is this not the wind of greedy disorder?
s0108.idiomatic: Is that not the breath of greedy disorder?

s0109.literal: Can it be a lofty precedent for today?
s0109.idiomatic: Can it be a lofty precedent for our age?

s0110.literal: As for the time when the Twin Peaks were both emperors and the four seas contended for supremacy—sometimes they allied with Zhao to invade Yan, sometimes they linked with Han to plot against Wei; bodies sought alliance in the hall of Chu, persons snatched the jade disk in the court of Qin; they sent the precious tripod to entrust it to the King of Qi, galloped the comfort carriage to lure a guest of Liang.
s0110.idiomatic: When the Twin Peaks were both emperors and the four seas fought for mastery, some allied with Zhao to strike Yan, some joined Han against Wei; men sought treaties in Chu's halls and snatched jade in Qin's court; they sent the sacred tripod to Qi and drove the comfort carriage to lure Liang's guest.

s0111.literal: Beyond that, oily lips and trafficking tongues, each taking a different road and whip, innocent and guiltless as brothers one to another.
s0111.idiomatic: Beyond that were slick tongues and peddled words, parting ways like brothers who were innocent alike.

s0112.literal: When Zhongyang received the Mandate, all under Heaven shared one measure; touring and inspecting the various Huaxia, none heard of hidden insult.
s0112.idiomatic: When Zhongyang received the Mandate, the realm shared one standard; in touring the Huaxia, none heard of secret humiliation.

s0113.literal: When the three sides were hegemons, Sun used sweet words to flatter, Cao bent deceit to tether; banners and chariots came yearly to Gouwú, caps and coaches raced yearly to Yong-Shu. Then guests' mockery was especially perilous, hosts' sport already deep; together they exhausted wandering talk—who said there was suspicion and offense?
s0113.idiomatic: Among the three hegemons, Sun flattered with honeyed words and Cao bound men with fraud; banners yearly reached Gouwú and coaches yearly sped to Yong-Shu. Guests' barbs grew sharp and hosts' games deep; they talked freely together—who spoke of suspicion?

s0114.literal: If one were to search out old precedents and there chanced to be earlier traces, I fear they would be the treacherous schemes of a decadent age, not winning policies for governing a state.
s0114.idiomatic: Search old precedents and any trace you find is likely a decadent age's treachery, not a state's winning strategy.

s0115.literal: Moreover I have heard: Cloud Master and Fire Emperor—their flood and purity differed in custom; dragon leaping and unicorn startling—king and hegemon though different in the Way, none failed to honor ruler and kin to inscribe things and thicken respect and nurture to govern the people. There were always state officers; never was there rise and fall.
s0115.idiomatic: I have also heard: Cloud Master and Fire Emperor differed in flood and purity; dragon and unicorn marked king and hegemon—yet all honored kin and ruler and thickened nurture to govern the people. States always had officers; ranks did not simply rise and fall.

s0116.literal: I have failed in warmth and coolness toward my parents and still belong to chaotic separation; bandits and foes run riot, public and private scattered in flight.
s0116.idiomatic: I have failed my parents in warmth and coolness and still live in chaos; enemies run wild and public and private life are scattered.

s0117.literal: The Xiao carriage has none to drive it; who holds the royal boat?
s0117.idiomatic: The imperial carriage lacks a driver; who holds the royal boat?

s0118.literal: Gazing toward home and native district—what heart remains for Heaven and Earth?
s0118.idiomatic: Gazing toward home—what heart is left for Heaven and Earth?

s0119.literal: Unless one were born leaning on barn bamboo and sprung from the hollow mulberry, travelers on the road would still feel compassion and pity one another.
s0119.idiomatic: Unless born of barn bamboo and hollow mulberry, wayfarers would still pity one another.

s0120.literal: I have always held that choosing an office to serve is not called filial to one's family; choosing an affair to hurry to is not said to be loyal to the state.
s0120.idiomatic: I have always held that choosing an office is not filial piety, and choosing an errand is not loyalty to the state.

s0121.literal: How much more when reverently receiving the Way and driving in the train of former kings—court gentlemen who understand the classics, owls and kites who know rites; touring the regions to transform custom, all inquire after the aged; eastern school and western academy all honor the old.
s0121.idiomatic: How much more when one reverently receives the Way and rides with former kings—clerks who know the classics, owls and kites who know ritual; tours to transform custom ask after the aged; eastern and western academies honor the old.

s0122.literal: I came with jade scepters and silks in friendly embassy; it happened to be a time of the world's hardship and struck the people's adverse fortune. For years piled on years I could not present the straight petition of the first month; swallowing tears and holding back sound, I long faced the public anger of the lanes. Pleas of feeling and rite would be like touching the inverse scale; words of loyalty and filial piety should all bite the tongue. This is what I did not plan for, not what I looked up to.
s0122.idiomatic: I came with jade and silk on friendly embassy, only to meet the world's hardship and the people's ill fortune. Year on year I could not file the New Year's straight petition; choking back tears I long faced public wrath. Pleas of feeling and rite would touch the dragon's scale; words of loyalty and filial piety must be bitten off. That is what I never planned and never hoped for.

s0123.literal: Moreover, love of Heaven's kin—how can it be forgotten from the heart?
s0123.idiomatic: And love of Heaven's kin—how can the heart forget it?

s0124.literal: Feeling for wife and children—who can be without burden?
s0124.idiomatic: Feeling for wife and children—who is without burden?

s0125.literal: Even the Princess of Qinghe in her nobility and the book-assistant's household of Yuyao, without limit of high or low, were all driven off and seized.
s0125.idiomatic: Even the Princess of Qinghe in her rank and the Yuyao clerk's household, high and low alike, were driven off and seized.

s0126.literal: Since the ugly foe of the southeast trafficked in starving people, terrace-office gentlemen were all starved against the walls; how much more my partings in life and death, many seasons of cold and heat, a widow's chamber and infant child—what words can tell it?
s0126.idiomatic: Since the southeast foe trafficked in the starving, terrace clerks starved against their walls; how much more my years of life-and-death parting, widow's room and infant—what words can tell it?

s0127.literal: If I could return in person to my native soil and search with my own hands, I would still hope to lead them by the hand and together escape cruel abuse.
s0127.idiomatic: If I could return home and search myself, I would still hope to lead them forth and together escape cruelty.

s0128.literal: When the Four Hearings do not reach, Huayang Jun called such men rebellious ministers; when the common people have no grievance, Sun Shu'ao was termed a good minister.
s0128.idiomatic: When the Four Hearings fail, Huayang Jun called that a rebellious minister; when the people have no wrongs, Sun Shu'ao was called a good minister.

s0129.literal: You, sir, have lofty talent and heavy reputation and assist in state policy—not leopard, not bear, you have heard the Odes and heard the Rites; yet on great deliberations of the central court you have never once argued with dignity; on fine plans of the clear forbidden precinct how could you reach them? Blunt bluntness is not Zhou She; easy compliance resembles Hu Guang—how is there no remonstrating minister?
s0129.idiomatic: You have lofty talent and weighty fame and assist state policy—you have heard Odes and Rites; yet on the court's great deliberations you have never argued; on the palace's fine plans how could you match them? Blunt speech is not Zhou She; easy compliance is Hu Guang—where are the remonstrating ministers?

s0130.literal: Years flow like water—how much of life remains? At dawn I watch the migrating geese and my heart races to the Jiang-Huai; at dusk I gaze at the Herd-Boy and feeling gallops to Yang-Yue. By day a thousand sorrows make me hide tears; by night ten thousand thoughts turn my entrails. I do not know myself as living; I do not know myself as dead.
s0130.idiomatic: Years flow like water—how much life is left? At dawn I watch wild geese and my heart flies to Jiang-Huai; at dusk I gaze at the Herd-Boy and feeling races to Yang-Yue. By day a thousand griefs bring tears; by night ten thousand thoughts wring the gut. I scarcely know I live; I scarcely know I die.

s0131.literal: You, sir, have always wielded a sharp edge in words and are also long in the cave of principle—Chancellor Kuang's brow-relaxing discourse, Magistrate Yue's ear-clearing talk; of what I have consulted and doubted, who can make it clear?
s0131.idiomatic: You have always had a sharp tongue and a deep grasp of principle—Chancellor Kuang's discourse that unknit the brow, Magistrate Yue's talk that cleared the ear; of my doubts, who can explain them?

s0132.literal: If my humble words are wrong, your coming letter will surely make it through; I ask only to be ashes and nails and gladly follow the axe and boiling cauldron—why merely stare in silence, bite the tongue, and bow the head?
s0132.idiomatic: If my words err, your reply will surely clear them; I ask only to be ashes under the nail and gladly face axe and cauldron—why only stare, bite my tongue, and bow my head?

s0133.literal: If one principle remains, I still hope for your compassionate regard—why must you expect that we shall surely die in the capital of Qi, that our feet tread the yellow dust of Zhao and Wei, that our bones add a sliver to You and Bing? Thus the bowing trees of Dongping would long cherish grief toward Han; the lonely tomb of western Luoyang would ever show dreams of longing for home.
s0133.idiomatic: If one point stands, I still hope for your mercy—why must you expect us to die in Qi's capital, feet in Zhao-Wei dust, bones adding to You-Bing? Then Dongping's bowing trees would long mourn toward Han; western Luoyang's lonely tomb would ever dream of home.

s0134.literal: Repeated pleas have made the choking grief deeper.
s0134.idiomatic: Repeated pleas have only deepened my choking grief.

s0135.literal: Zunyian in the end did not reply to the letter.

s0136.literal: When Jiangling fell, Qi sent the Marquis of Zhenyuan Xiao Yuanming as Liang successor, and then dispatched Ling to return with him.
s0136.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Qi sent the Marquis of Zhenyuan, Xiao Yuanming, as Liang successor and had Ling accompany him back.

s0137.literal: Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian at first barred the border and would not receive them; Yuanming sent letters back and forth, all in Ling's wording.
s0137.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian at first barred the border and refused entry; Yuanming exchanged letters, all drafted by Ling.

s0138.literal: When Yuanming entered, Sengbian was greatly delighted to obtain Ling, received and entertained him with gifts—his courtesy was very generous.
s0138.idiomatic: When Yuanming entered, Sengbian was overjoyed to have Ling, entertained him generously, and heaped gifts upon him.

s0139.literal: Ling was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, in charge of edicts and proclamations.
s0139.idiomatic: Ling was made director of the ministry of personnel in the masters of writing and handled edicts.

s0140.literal: That year the Founder led troops to execute Sengbian and then advanced to attack Wei Zai.
s0140.idiomatic: That year the Founder led troops to kill Sengbian and then marched against Wei Zai.

s0141.literal: At that time Ren Yue and Xu Sihui seized the moment to raid Stone City; Ling, moved by Sengbian's old kindness, then went to join Yue.
s0141.idiomatic: At that time Ren Yue and Xu Sihui raided Stone City; Ling, remembering Sengbian's kindness, went to join Yue.

s0142.literal: When Yue and the others were pacified, the Founder released Ling without inquiry.
s0142.idiomatic: When Yue and the rest were subdued, the Founder pardoned Ling without punishment.

s0143.literal: Soon afterward he was made Zhenwei General and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
s0143.idiomatic: He was soon made zhenwei general and left vice director of the masters of writing.

s0144.literal: In the second year of Shaotai he was again sent as envoy to Qi; on return he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presenting Matters and Director of the Secretariat.
s0144.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2 (555) he was again envoy to Qi; on return he was made attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate for presenting matters and director of the secretariat.

s0145.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry while the left vice director post remained as before.
s0145.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Ling was also made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry while keeping the left vice director post.

s0146.literal: At the beginning of Tianjia he was made Minister of the Grand Storehouse.
s0146.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjia (560) he was made minister of the grand storehouse.

s0147.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to Minister of the Five Arms and concurrently Grand Director of Composition.
s0147.idiomatic: In year 4 he was moved to minister of the five arms and concurrently grand director of composition.

s0148.literal: In the sixth year he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
s0148.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and imperial censor-in-chief.

s0149.literal: At that time the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, was Minister of Works; by the emperor's younger-brother rank his power bent the court.
s0149.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, was minister of works; as the emperor's brother his power dominated the court.

s0150.literal: Straight guard Bao Sengrui borrowed the prince's authority, blocked and choked lawsuits, and great ministers dared not speak.
s0150.idiomatic: Straight guard Bao Sengrui used the prince's power to choke off lawsuits, and great ministers dared not speak.

s0151.literal: When Ling heard of it, he drew up a memorial of impeachment, led attendants from the Southern Terrace, and entered presenting the case.
s0151.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Ling drafted an impeachment memorial, led Southern Terrace attendants, and entered with the case.

s0152.literal: Emperor Wen saw Ling's memorial and bearing stern, as if he could not be violated, and composed his face to sit upright.
s0152.idiomatic: Emperor Wen saw Ling's stern memorial and bearing, as though he could not be touched, and straightened himself on the throne.

s0153.literal: When Ling advanced to read the memorial board, the Prince of Ancheng stood attending in the hall, looking up at the emperor, sweating and losing color.
s0153.idiomatic: As Ling read the memorial, the Prince of Ancheng stood in the hall, looked up at the emperor, and sweated pale.

s0154.literal: Ling sent a palace censor to lead the prince down from the hall and then impeached and removed him from attendant-in-ordinary and director of the secretariat.
s0154.idiomatic: Ling had a palace censor lead the prince down and impeached him from attendant-in-ordinary and director of the secretariat.

s0155.literal: From this the court was awed into order.
s0155.idiomatic: From then the court was awed into order.

s0156.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he was moved to Minister of Personnel and concurrently Grand Director of Composition.
s0156.idiomatic: In Tiankang year 1 (566) he was moved to minister of personnel and concurrently grand director of composition.

s0157.literal: Ling, because from the end of Liang appointments and grants had mostly missed their proper targets, then raised the guiding cords and examined names against reality.
s0157.idiomatic: Because since late Liang appointments had missed their mark, Ling raised standards and matched names to reality.

s0158.literal: At that time there were those who pushed forward rashly seeking office, clamoring without cease; Ling then issued a written proclamation, saying: "From antiquity those who were Ministers of Personnel assessed human relations, selected talent, traced lineage, followed great and small, and measured rank and title.
s0158.idiomatic: When men clamored for office without end, Ling issued a proclamation: "From antiquity the minister of personnel assessed men, chose talent, traced lineage, weighed rank, and measured office.

s0159.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang inherited Hou Jing's cruel desolation; Grand Marshal Wang received Jingzhou's disaster and defeat—at that time mourning and chaos left no regulations, and so official ranks reached this tangle.
s0159.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang inherited Hou Jing's ruin; Grand Marshal Wang took Jingzhou's disaster—then mourning and chaos left no rules, and offices fell into this tangle.

s0160.literal: In the time of Yongding the holy court was newly founded, war had not ceased, and there was likewise no order.
s0160.idiomatic: In Yongding the new court was still at war and likewise had no order.

s0161.literal: Treasury and storehouses were empty, rewards hung lacking; white silver was hard to obtain, yellow edicts easy to arrange—rank was used in place of cash and silk to comfort and connect, with no reckoning of amount, so that supernumerary attendants and regular attendants stood shoulder to shoulder on the road, consultants and staff officers were countless in the market. Was this what court regulations should be?
s0161.idiomatic: Treasuries were empty and rewards scarce; white silver was hard to get and yellow edicts easy to trade—rank stood in for cash to comfort men, with no count of numbers, until supernumerary and regular attendants crowded the roads and consultants and staff officers filled the markets. Was that what court law should be?

s0162.literal: Now caps, robes, rites, and music grow richer year by year—how can the old way still be followed? It is not reasonable expectation.
s0162.idiomatic: Now rites and music grow richer each year—how can the old way still hold? That is not reasonable.

s0163.literal: Those I see, gentlemen, mostly exceed their proper measure and still say they suffer great constraint—they do not understand your lofty intent.
s0163.idiomatic: Most of you exceed your proper rank and still call it great constraint—you do not grasp your superiors' intent.

s0164.literal: If one asks whether Zhu Yijun of Liang also became minister and chancellor—did he not exceed his measure?
s0164.idiomatic: If you ask whether Liang's Zhu Yijun also became minister and chancellor—did he not exceed his measure?

s0165.literal: That was the Son of Heaven's elevation; it had nothing to do with the selection sequence.
s0165.idiomatic: That was the Son of Heaven's choice, not the selection process.

s0166.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said, "Men of the world speak of having an eye for men; I alone have no eye for Fan Ti."
s0166.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang said, "The world speaks of an eye for men; I alone have no eye for Fan Ti."

s0167.literal: Emperor Wen of Song also said, "Does the human world lack fate? Whenever a fine office is vacant I always think of Yang Xuanbao."
s0167.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song also said, "Does the world lack fate? Whenever a fine post opens I think of Yang Xuanbao."

s0168.literal: Thus clear ranks and conspicuous posts do not come through selection.
s0168.idiomatic: Thus high offices do not come through selection.

s0169.literal: In Qin the carriage-office director Zhao Gao rose straight to chancellor; in Han the high-temple director Tian Qianqiu also became chancellor—can these again serve as examples?
s0169.idiomatic: In Qin the carriage-office director Zhao Gao rose to chancellor; in Han the high-temple director Tian Qianqiu did the same—are those examples?

s0170.literal: Having been entrusted with the current, one ought to apply ink.
s0170.idiomatic: Having charge of the current, I must apply the ink.

s0171.literal: What I hope from you gentlemen is a deep understanding of my humble intent.
s0171.idiomatic: I ask you gentlemen to understand my intent deeply.

s0172.literal: " From this all submitted in admiration; opinion of the time compared him to Mao Jie.
s0172.idiomatic: " Thereafter all submitted; contemporaries compared him to Mao Jie.

s0173.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Emperor Xuan entered to assist and, plotting to remove those of divergent intent, drew Ling into the deliberation.
s0173.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Emperor Xuan entered as regent and, planning to remove dissenters, drew Ling into counsel.

s0174.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the calendar, he enfeoffed Ling as Marquis of Jianchang with a fief of five hundred households.
s0174.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he enfeoffed Ling as Marquis of Jianchang, fief five hundred households.

s0175.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
s0175.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 (569) he was made right vice director of the masters of writing.

s0176.literal: In the third year he was moved to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
s0176.idiomatic: In year 3 he was moved to left vice director of the masters of writing.

s0177.literal: Ling submitted a memorial declining in favor of Zhou Hongzheng, Wang Li, and others. Emperor Xuan summoned Ling into the inner hall and said, "Why do you stubbornly decline this post and recommend others?"
s0177.idiomatic: Ling memorialized to yield to Zhou Hongzheng, Wang Li, and others. Emperor Xuan summoned him and said, "Why stubbornly decline and recommend others?"

s0178.literal: Ling said, "Zhou Hongzheng returned west with Your Majesty and was long the chief clerk of the old fief; Wang Li was chief clerk of the Taiping chancellor's office; Zhang Zhong is a worthy kinsman of the imperial district. If one chooses worthies of old service, I should stand behind."
s0178.idiomatic: Ling said, "Zhou Hongzheng came west with Your Majesty and was long chief clerk of the old fief; Wang Li was chief clerk of the Taiping chancellor's office; Zhang Zhong is an imperial kinsman. Choose worthies of old service and I should stand behind."

s0179.literal: For days he stubbornly declined; Emperor Xuan urgently charged him, and Ling then accepted the edict.
s0179.idiomatic: He declined for days; Emperor Xuan pressed him, and Ling accepted the edict.

s0180.literal: When the court deliberated a northern expedition, Emperor Xuan said, "My mind is already decided—you may nominate a commander-in-chief."
s0180.idiomatic: When court debated a northern campaign, Emperor Xuan said, "My mind is set—nominate a commander."

s0181.literal: In joint deliberation all thought Central Authority General Chunyu Liang, because of his weighty position, and together signed to push him.
s0181.idiomatic: All thought Central Authority General Chunyu Liang weighty and jointly recommended him.

s0182.literal: Ling alone said, "It is not so.

s0183.literal: Wu Mingche's family lies on the Huai's left; he knows their customs thoroughly, and in generalship and talent there is today none who surpasses him."
s0183.idiomatic: Wu Mingche is from the Huai region, knows their ways, and in talent and generalship none today surpasses him."

s0184.literal: Thereupon debate piled up for days without decision.
s0184.idiomatic: Debate then lasted days without decision.

s0185.literal: Minister of Justice Pei Ji said, "Your subject agrees with Vice Director Xu."
s0185.idiomatic: Minister of justice Pei Ji said, "I agree with Vice Director Xu."

s0186.literal: Ling answered on the spot, "Not only is Mingche a fine general—Pei Ji is himself a fine deputy."
s0186.idiomatic: Ling answered at once, "Mingche is a fine general—and Pei Ji is a fine deputy."

s0187.literal: That day an edict made Mingche Grand Commander-in-Chief and ordered Ji to oversee military affairs; they then took several tens of Huainan commanderies.
s0187.idiomatic: That day Mingche was made grand commander and Ji ordered to oversee the army; they then took dozens of Huainan prefectures.

s0188.literal: Emperor Xuan then set out wine, raised his cup, and charged Ling, saying, "I reward you for knowing men."
s0188.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then raised his cup to Ling: "I reward you for knowing men."

s0189.literal: Ling left his mat and replied, "The decision came from Your Majesty's sacred mind—it is not this subject's strength."
s0189.idiomatic: Ling left his mat and said, "The decision was Your Majesty's—not my strength."

s0190.literal: That year he was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary; the rest remained as before.
s0190.idiomatic: That year he was also made attendant-in-ordinary; the rest unchanged.

s0191.literal: In the seventh year he concurrently held Director of the National University and Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou.
s0191.idiomatic: In year 7 he also held director of the national university and grand arbiter of South Xuzhou.

s0192.literal: Because of public business he was removed from attendant-in-ordinary and vice director.
s0192.idiomatic: On public business he was removed from attendant-in-ordinary and vice director.

s0193.literal: Soon he was again made attendant-in-ordinary, granted a staff for support, and again made Commander of the Palace Guards.
s0193.idiomatic: Soon he was again attendant-in-ordinary, given a support staff, and again commander of the palace guards.

s0194.literal: In the eighth year he was additionally made Right Supporting General and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with assistant clerks appointed.
s0194.idiomatic: In year 8 he was also right supporting general and grand tutor of the heir apparent, with assistant clerks.

s0195.literal: Before long he was moved to Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; the rest remained as before.
s0195.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to right grand master for splendid happiness; the rest unchanged.

s0196.literal: In the tenth year he again became Commander of the Palace Guards.
s0196.idiomatic: In year 10 he again became commander of the palace guards.

s0197.literal: Soon afterward he was moved to Pacifying Right General and Magistrate of Danyang.
s0197.idiomatic: Soon he was made pacifying right general and magistrate of Danyang.

s0198.literal: In the thirteenth year he was made Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granted one set of martial music, while attendant-in-ordinary, general, right grand master, and grand arbiter remained as before.
s0198.idiomatic: In year 13 he was director of the secretariat, concurrently grand tutor of the heir apparent, granted martial music; attendant, general, right grand master, and grand arbiter unchanged.

s0199.literal: Ling, because of age, repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; Emperor Xuan also treated him generously and then ordered the director of palace construction to build a great fast and had Ling conduct affairs at his residence.
s0199.idiomatic: Ling, being old, repeatedly asked to retire; Emperor Xuan favored him and ordered the director of palace construction to build a great fast hall so Ling could conduct business at home.

s0200.literal: When Houzhu ascended, Ling was moved to Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the rest remained as before.
s0200.idiomatic: When Houzhu ascended, Ling was moved to left grand master for splendid happiness and junior tutor of the heir apparent; the rest unchanged.
